description: Composite figure of seven parts mixing SEM micrographs, EDS maps, an XRD pattern, micro-CT reconstructions and two histograms, all characterising the initial microstructure of the present steel. (a) Pseudo-3D SEM block image showing three orthogonal surfaces of the specimen, with the axes RD, TD and ND marked and arrows labelling "Primary TiB₂" (top face) and "Eutectic TiB₂" (side faces); scale bar 100 μm; dark particulate contrast in a light matrix. (b) High-magnification SEM of the RD surface with a red-boxed region and a black-framed enlarged inset; bars labelled 50 μm and 5 μm (inset), ND and TD axes indicated; angular to plate-like dark particles. (c) High-magnification SEM in which dashed red lines separate regions labelled "Ferrite" and "Austenite", with an inset giving Mn (green) and Al (orange/yellow) EDS maps; scale bar 2 μm. (d) XRD pattern, intensity (a.u.) versus 2θ = 30–100°, with peaks indexed for δ-ferrite (black), austenite (blue) and TiB₂ (red). (e) Four micro-CT particle reconstructions of one volume, colour-coded by equivalent diameter in the 0.8–5.0, 5.0–10.0, 10.0–20.0 and 20.0–42.7 μm domains; 200 μm scale bars. (f) and (g) bar charts of particle number fraction and volume fraction versus equivalent-diameter bins. Together the panels establish a TiB₂-reinforced ferrite–austenite microstructure in which coarse particles dominate by volume.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a pseudo-3D SEM block image of three orthogonal surfaces of the specimen with the axes RD, TD and ND drawn as arrows and a 100 μm scale bar; two families of dark particles are arrow-labelled 'Primary TiB₂' and 'Eutectic TiB₂'.

Panel (b) shows the RD surface at high magnification with a red rectangular region and a black-framed enlarged inset; two scale bars are printed, 50 μm and 5 μm for the inset, and the ND/TD directions are marked.
Panel (c) uses dashed red lines to separate two microstructural regions labelled 'Ferrite' and 'Austenite', and carries an inset of Mn (green) and Al (orange) EDS maps; the scale bar is 2 μm.

Panel (d) is an XRD pattern over 2θ = 30–100° (intensity in a.u.) with the legend 'δ-Ferrite' (black), 'Austenite' (blue) and 'TiB₂' (red); red TiB₂ reflections 1010, 10-11, 211-0, 202-0 and 202-1 and black δ-ferrite reflections 110, 200, 211 are indexed alongside blue austenite reflections 111, 200, 220, 311, 222.

Panel (e) consists of four micro-CT reconstructions of the same volume, each with a colour bar whose printed values are 0.8–5.0, 5.0–10.0, 10.0–20.0 and 20.0–42.7 respectively, and each with a 200 μm scale bar.

In panel (e), the low-diameter (0.8–5.0) map is uniformly speckled throughout the volume, while the largest-diameter (20.0–42.7) map contains only sparse, isolated bright spots, so small particles are numerous but coarse particles are few in number.

Panel (f), particle number fraction vs equivalent diameter, peaks at the (0.8, 5] bin (bar top between the 40 and 50 % gridlines) and falls progressively through (5, 10], (10, 20] to a near-zero (20, 42.7] bar.

Panel (g), particle volume fraction vs equivalent diameter, peaks at the (10, 20] bin (between 50 and 60 %), with (20, 42.7] at roughly 30–40 %, (5, 10] at about 10 % and (0.8, 5] near zero — the opposite ranking to panel (f).

The caption states that particles in different size domains in (e) were measured by computerized tomography and that (f) and (g) give particle size distributions in terms of number fractions and volume fractions respectively.

The caption states that (c) is a high-magnification SEM image with dashed red lines delineating the Mn-rich austenite and Al-rich ferrite regions, and that (a) is a representative pseudo 3D SEM image of the surface in three different directions.
The citing text states that the area fraction of particles (dark contrast in Fig. 4(a)) is 9.6 % from the RD surface and 13.4 % from the ND surface, consistent with 12.5 % measured by XRD.
The citing text states that the particles were verified as TiB₂ by the XRD analysis in Fig. 4(d) and that the XRD result also uncovers the ferrite–austenite dual-phase nature of the matrix.

The citing text states the TiB₂ particle size falls within 2.4–35 μm with an average value of 15 μm, whereas the micro-CT bin edges shown in (e)–(g) span 0.8–42.7 μm; the two ranges are not identical.

The citing text states that micro-CT analysis (Fig. 4(e–g)) reveals small particles (0.8–5.0 μm) prevail in numbers while coarse particles (10.0–42.7 μm) govern the microstructure by accounting for >80 % of the total area fraction of particles.
The citing text states that Mn and Al are partitioned into different grains in the matrix region shown in the inset of Fig. 4(c), as confirmed by EDS elemental mapping.

subfigures.description: Pseudo-3D SEM block image of three orthogonal surfaces (RD, TD, ND) of the present steel; dark particles in a light matrix, with arrows labelling 'Primary TiB₂' on the top face and 'Eutectic TiB₂' on the side faces; scale bar 100 μm.

High-magnification SEM of the RD surface; a red box marks a region reproduced in the black-framed inset. Two scale bars are printed, 50 μm and 5 μm (inset); ND and TD axes are indicated by arrows. Angular, plate-like and blocky dark particles are dispersed in the matrix.

High-magnification SEM with dashed red lines delineating regions labelled 'Ferrite' and 'Austenite'; a boxed inset shows Mn (green, top) and Al (orange, bottom) EDS maps of the same area. Scale bar 2 μm.

XRD pattern, intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ = 30–100°. Legend identifies δ-Ferrite (black), Austenite (blue) and TiB₂ (red). Indexed reflections include 1010, 10-11, 211-0, 202-0, 202-1 (TiB₂, red); 110, 200, 211 (δ-ferrite, black); 111, 200, 220, 311, 222 (austenite, blue).

Set of four micro-CT particle reconstructions of the same specimen volume, each with its own colour bar labelled 0.8–5.0, 5.0–10.0, 10.0–20.0 and 20.0–42.7 (no unit printed on the bar); 200 μm scale bar beneath each map. The 0.8–5.0 map is densely speckled over the whole volume, whereas the 20.0–42.7 map shows sparse isolated high-value spots.

Bar chart of particle number fraction (%) vs equivalent diameter (μm) with bins (0.8, 5], (5, 10], (10, 20], (20, 42.7]. The (0.8, 5] bar is tallest (between the 40 and 50 gridlines), followed by (5, 10] (between 20 and 30, nearer 30), then (10, 20] (just below 25), and a very small (20, 42.7] bar near 0–5.

Bar chart of particle volume fraction (%) vs equivalent diameter (μm) with the same bins. The (10, 20] bar is tallest (between 50 and 60), (20, 42.7] is next (between 30 and 40, about one third), (5, 10] is around 10 and (0.8, 5] is near zero.

unreadable_items: the colour-bar axis titles of the four micro-CT maps in (e): the top of each colour bar is cropped so the quantity/unit label is illegible (only numeric values 0.8–5.0, 5.0–10.0, 10.0–20.0, 20.0–42.7 are readable); the caption fragment suggests 'Equivalent diameter (μm)'
panel letters of the four micro-CT maps in (e) are cropped/not individually visible, so the assignment of each map to a size domain rests on its colour bar values
fine particle morphology and any particle-size annotation inside panel (b) inset
exact bar heights in (f) and (g): readable only relative to gridlines, not as printed numeric labels
